thread:
lee_support: FYI SilverRidge is seeing p95/p99 regressions on the /v1/embeddings endpoint since ~04:15 UTC. Customer reports a lot of queued requests and timeouts. They pasted a trace and some logs.

sara_cs: Thanks — can you attach the traces and whether they have a reservation or priority lane? Also what model/quant profile they're using?

lee_support: Pasted trace excerpt below (customer sent). No reservation. Model: embed-large-quant. Workload is bulk batch uploads (many small requests).

```
2026-03-17T04:18:02Z [sr-42] req_id=abc123 queued_ms=420 cpu_steal_pct=38 kernel_wait_ms=12 shard=gpu-pool-7
2026-03-17T04:18:02Z [sr-42] req_id=abc124 queued_ms=112 cpu_steal_pct=12 kernel_wait_ms=2 shard=gpu-pool-7
2026-03-17T04:19:10Z [sr-42] req_id=abc200 queued_ms=860 cpu_steal_pct=52 kernel_wait_ms=30 shard=gpu-pool-7
```

mike_oncall: Looking at infra metrics now. I can see a short noisy burst from tenant sr-42 spiking queued_time and CPU steal on gpu-pool-7. Several other tenants on that pool were impacted (p95 up across the pool).

nate_sre: Can you run a quick query for per-tenant QPS / active sessions on that shard? Also check if our batching heuristics created oversized microbatches that pushed kernel contention.

mike_oncall: Running: `rbctl metrics query --shard gpu-pool-7 --metric queued_ms, cpu_steal_pct --group tenant --since 30m` — result: sr-42 accounted for ~62% of queued_ms during spike window, QPS ~48, bursty pattern with lots of short-lived concurrent streams.

sara_cs: Customer says these are parallel small file uploads from their ingest pipeline. They don't have throttles on their side. We should offer a short-term mitigation and a longer-term plan (reservation or compacting requests).

lee_support: Proposed short-term: (1) Temp per-tenant throttle to smooth bursts, (2) offer 2-hour ephemeral reservation + migrate them to another less-busy pool, (3) suggest client-side batching changes. Thoughts?

nate_sre: Agree. For immediate relief I'd do ephemeral reservation + a conservative per-tenant QPS cap (e.g., 15 rps) for 30m while reservation warms up. Reservation avoids noisy neighbor on same pool.

katie_prodinfra: I can create an ephemeral reservation and push a soft throttle. Need approval for reservation capacity and to notify ops. Command I'll run: `rbctl reservations create --tenant sr-42 --capacity 20rps --duration 2h --shard prefer:gpu-pool-12 --metadata "ephemeral_support_mitigation"`

lee_support: Go ahead. Tell them it's temporary and we'll monitor. Sara, can you confirm with customer that we will do a 2h reservation + soft throttle 15rps now?

sara_cs: Confirmed with customer — they accept temporary reservation and will try to adjust client side after.

katie_prodinfra: Pushing reservation now.

deploy-bot: reservation-service: created reservation res-20260317-789 for tenant sr-42 (20rps, 2h) -> target shard gpu-pool-12

katie_prodinfra: Also applying soft throttle rule: `routing.policy.add --tenant sr-42 --max-rps 15 --priority soft` — applied.

nate_sre: Seeing immediate effect on gpu-pool-7: queued_ms dropping, cpu_steal percentage trending down. Will continue to watch for 15m.

mike_oncall: Quick sanity: p95 for /embeddings for sr-42 pre-mitigation ~1.2s, p99 ~4.8s. After reservation+throttle: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~720ms (initial). Marking mitigation effective.

sara_cs: Passing update to SilverRidge — they reported fewer timeouts and faster responses. They asked whether this will be permanent; we told them ops will propose a plan (reservation vs. priority lane purchase vs. partitioning jobs).

lee_support: Follow-ups: - Nate to run a root cause post-check for batching behavior and kernel contention. - Product infra to recommend a long-term SKU for bulk ingest (reserved capacity or burst credits). - CS to coordinate with customer on client-side batching (suggest 5s client-side coalescing).

nate_sre: I'll collect traces and kernel contention logs and post a short postmortem in #eng-sre by EOD. Initial hypothesis: high parallel small requests caused intermittent kernel scheduler contention + host-level CPU steal from other co-located system jobs.

katie_prodinfra: Reservation res-20260317-789 scheduled to expire in 2h; I'll open a follow-up ticket to either extend or migrate to a formal Dedicated contract if both sides agree.

sara_cs: Customer grateful. Mark this thread resolved from support POV; will reopen if they see new regressions.

lee_support: Thanks all — great triage. :thumbsup:
